articles.title: A Greener City, a Better Life
articles.subtitle: 城市的绿色空间，如何改变日常生活？
articles.provenance: AI 原创示例 · 2026-10-10 · 学习用途，非官方真题

paragraphs.english: As cities expand, a growing population puts pressure on land, housing and transport. Urban planners often face a difficult choice: should an empty site become another office building or a public park? A park may appear less profitable, yet its contribution to residents' well-being can be considerable. Green spaces offer a place to exercise, meet neighbours and escape the noise of crowded streets. For people living in small flats, access to a nearby garden can make everyday life more pleasant.
paragraphs.chinese: 随着城市扩张，人口增长给土地、住房和交通带来压力。城市规划者常常面临选择：空地应该建办公楼还是公园？公园看似利润较低，却能明显改善居民的身心状态。对住在小公寓里的人来说，附近的花园能让生活更加舒适。

paragraphs.english: Trees also play a practical role. Their shade can reduce the heat people experience on a summer afternoon, while soil allows some rainfall to soak into the ground. A sustainable design considers these benefits alongside maintenance costs. However, planting a few trees is not a complete solution to pollution or flooding. Effective policy needs evidence, careful planning and long-term investment. Local authorities should assess each neighbourhood rather than assume that one design will work everywhere.
paragraphs.chinese: 树木也发挥着实际作用。树荫能减轻夏日下午的炎热，土壤则让一部分雨水渗入地下。可持续设计要兼顾这些益处与维护成本，但种几棵树不能彻底解决污染或洪涝问题。有效政策需要证据、细致规划和长期投入，并评估各个社区的实际情况。

paragraphs.english: Another concern is inequality. Wealthier districts may enjoy attractive parks, whereas disadvantaged communities have fewer safe places to relax. To promote fair access, a city could prioritise areas with limited facilities and involve residents in decisions. This approach helps preserve local knowledge and builds a sense of responsibility. Ultimately, a successful green project is not measured only by the number of trees planted. It should improve the environment while responding to the needs of the people who use it.
paragraphs.chinese: 另一个问题是资源不平等。较富裕的地区可能拥有漂亮的公园，而弱势社区缺少安全的休闲场所。城市可以优先改善设施不足的地区，并让居民参与决策。成功的绿化项目不只看种了多少树，还要改善环境并回应使用者的需求。

questions.explanation: 第一段指出，公园对居民身心状态的作用可以相当显著，并提供锻炼和社交空间。

options: Every neighbourhood needs the same design.

questions.explanation: 第二段明确说明，种几棵树不能彻底解决污染或洪涝；设计需要评估各地需求。

options: Prioritise only wealthy districts.

questions.explanation: 第三段建议优先改善设施不足的地区，并让居民参与决策。

articles.title: Learning Beyond the Classroom
articles.subtitle: 技能会变化，学习也不必止于毕业。
articles.provenance: AI 原创示例 · 2026-10-10 · 学习用途，非官方真题

paragraphs.english: For many people, education once meant attending school and obtaining a qualification before entering employment. Today, technological change can alter the skills a job requires within a few years. An employee who could previously rely on familiar methods may need to adapt to new software or work with colleagues in different countries. Lifelong learning offers a way to respond to this uncertainty. It does not always require a university degree: a short course, a practical workshop or guided practice can also be useful.
paragraphs.chinese: 对许多人来说，教育曾意味着上学、获得资格，然后就业。如今，技术变化可能在几年内改变一份工作所需的技能。终身学习能帮助人们应对这种不确定性，也不一定意味着攻读大学学位：短期课程、实践工作坊或有指导的练习同样有用。

paragraphs.english: Online courses provide flexibility, especially for adults balancing work and family responsibilities. Learners can choose a convenient time and repeat difficult lessons. Nevertheless, convenience alone does not guarantee progress. Motivation often declines when a course feels disconnected from real life. To acquire a skill effectively, learners need clear goals, regular feedback and opportunities to apply what they have studied. A person learning to write reports, for instance, might practise with a realistic task instead of simply watching more videos.
paragraphs.chinese: 在线课程为兼顾工作与家庭的成年人提供了灵活性，但便利本身不能保证进步。当课程与现实脱节时，学习动力往往会下降。有效掌握技能需要明确目标、定期反馈和实践机会。例如，学习报告写作的人可以练习真实任务，而不只是不断观看视频。

paragraphs.english: Employers have a role as well. If training is available only outside working hours, some staff may struggle to participate. Organisations can allocate time for learning and encourage experienced workers to share expertise. Such support may strengthen confidence and help a team solve unfamiliar problems. However, responsibility should not fall entirely on individuals or businesses. Public libraries and community centres can offer affordable resources, making learning more inclusive. The broader aim is not merely to increase productivity, but to enable people to make informed choices throughout their lives.
paragraphs.chinese: 雇主也有责任。如果培训只能在下班后进行，一些员工可能难以参加。组织可以安排学习时间，鼓励经验丰富的员工分享专业知识。图书馆和社区中心也可提供价格合理的资源，让学习更包容。学习的目标不仅是提高生产效率，也包括帮助人们一生中作出知情的选择。

The programme creates employment opportunities.
Workers need time to adapt to new systems.

Remote courses provide greater flexibility.
Small goals can help learners maintain motivation.

Managers should allocate time for training.
Experienced teachers share their expertise.
Inclusive education responds to different needs.

questions.prompt: What is the author's view of lifelong learning?
options: It always requires a degree.
It can take several practical forms.
It is useful only before employment.
questions.explanation: 第一段列出短期课程、工作坊和有指导的练习，表明终身学习有多种形式。

questions.prompt: Why might motivation decline in an online course?
options: The course seems disconnected from real life.
The learner receives regular feedback.
The learner applies a skill to a real task.
questions.explanation: 第二段指出课程与现实脱节时，学习动力往往会下降。

questions.prompt: Which action is recommended for employers?
options: Place all responsibility on employees.
Provide training only after work.
Allocate time for learning.
questions.explanation: 第三段建议组织分配学习时间，并支持员工分享专业知识。

articles.title: The Value of Our Attention
articles.subtitle: 在数字生活中，为专注留一点空间。
articles.provenance: AI 原创示例 · 2026-10-10 · 学习用途，非官方真题

paragraphs.english: Digital devices have transformed the way people communicate and obtain information. A message can reach a friend in seconds, and a student can explore a vast range of learning materials without leaving home. Yet the same devices may interrupt activities that require concentration. Notifications compete for attention, encouraging users to switch between a task and a screen. The issue is not simply how much time people spend online, but whether their habits support the activities they consider important.
paragraphs.chinese: 数字设备改变了人们沟通和获取信息的方式，却也可能打断需要专注的活动。通知争夺注意力，促使用户在任务和屏幕之间切换。问题不只是花了多少时间上网，还包括使用习惯是否支持自己真正重视的事情。

paragraphs.english: One possible strategy is to establish boundaries. Someone working on a demanding assignment could silence unnecessary alerts and set aside a period for checking messages. This approach aims to minimise distraction while preserving the benefits of communication. It is also useful to evaluate which applications deserve frequent use. An application that helps a person maintain relationships serves a different purpose from one opened automatically whenever there is a spare moment. Recognising that distinction can make decisions more deliberate.
paragraphs.chinese: 一种策略是建立界限。处理复杂任务时，可以关闭不必要的提醒，并安排专门时间查看消息。这样既能减少干扰，又能保留沟通的好处。我们也可以评估哪些应用值得频繁使用，区分主动维护关系与空闲时下意识打开应用，让选择更加有意识。

paragraphs.english: Personal habits, however, are only part of the picture. Designers can influence behaviour through default settings and the way information is presented. A service that offers clear controls may help users manage their experience, whereas a confusing interface can make that harder. Greater transparency about recommendations could support informed choices. There is no single routine that suits everyone: a parent, a student and a shift worker have different needs. A balanced relationship with technology therefore depends on both thoughtful design and individual reflection, rather than on the assumption that every digital activity is harmful.
paragraphs.chinese: 个人习惯只是问题的一部分。设计者也会通过默认设置和信息呈现方式影响行为。清晰的控制选项与推荐机制透明度有助于用户作出知情的选择。适合每个人的统一日程并不存在，因此平衡的数字生活需要良好设计与个人反思。

vocabulary.example: Online tools have transformed the way teams collaborate.
Reading a complex argument requires concentration.
Planning breaks can be an effective strategy.
Families can establish clear boundaries for device use.
A quiet workspace helps minimise distraction.
Turning off alerts may reduce distraction.
Users should evaluate the benefits of each tool.
There is a distinction between useful breaks and constant interruption.
She made a deliberate choice to check messages later.
Default settings can influence behaviour.
Greater transparency helps users understand recommendations.
The report challenges the assumption that all screen time is alike.

questions.prompt: What does the author say matters besides time spent online?
options: Whether habits support important activities.
The price of a person's device.
How many apps a person owns.
questions.explanation: 第一段强调，应考虑数字使用习惯是否支持自己重视的活动，而不只计算上网时间。

questions.prompt: Which action is suggested to minimise distraction?
options: Check every notification immediately.
Silence unnecessary alerts during demanding work.
Avoid all communication permanently.
questions.explanation: 第二段建议在复杂任务期间关闭不必要的提醒，同时安排时间处理消息。

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the final paragraph?
options: Every person should follow the same routine.
All digital activity is harmful.
Both design and individual reflection matter.
questions.explanation: 最后一段说明，个人需求不同，平衡的数字生活取决于良好设计与个人反思。

articles.title: Small Steps: Better Bus Journeys
articles.subtitle: 公交出行与可靠的日常安排
articles.provenance: AI 原创分级练习 · 2026-10-12 · 情境结尾与题目修订；难度未作教学标定

paragraphs.english: A town wants more people to use its bus service. In this example, a student named Leo travels to college each morning. He checks the timetable before he leaves home. A bus with a clear route can take him close to the library. If the service is reliable, he does not need his family to drive him every day.
paragraphs.chinese: 在这个例子中，小镇希望更多人乘公交。学生 Leo 每天去学院，出门前查看时刻表。清晰的线路能把他送到图书馆附近，可靠的服务也能减少家人接送的需要。

paragraphs.english: Leo and his neighbours keep a record of late buses for one week. They send it to the local transport office and ask for a better timetable. The office can listen to the people who use the service. However, a new route may need more drivers and money. A useful decision must consider these limits as well as the passengers' wishes.
paragraphs.chinese: Leo 和邻居记录了一周的公交晚点情况，向交通部门提出改进建议。但新线路可能需要更多司机和资金，决策必须兼顾限制与乘客需求。

paragraphs.english: People can choose a plan and share a question before they act. The aim is to learn from what happens. A small benefit is still useful, and they can change the next step. A timetable is useful only if the bus usually arrives close to the listed time. Recording the same morning journey again would show whether Leo can reach college more reliably, rather than merely whether a new timetable has been printed.
paragraphs.chinese: 人们可以在行动前选择计划、提出并分享问题。目标是从结果中学习，小益处也有价值，之后可以调整下一步。时刻表只有在公交通常按所列时间到达时才有用。再次记录同一趟早班车，可以判断 Leo 是否更能准时到校，而不只是确认是否印了新时刻表。

paragraphs.english: A teacher returns a student's short essay with several comments. At first, the student looks only at the mark. paragraphs.english: The student rewrites the paragraph and compares the two versions. She keeps the part that already works and changes the sentences that confuse the reader. A manageable goal may help more than a long list of faults without any explanation of what to do next.
paragraphs.chinese: 学生重写段落、比较两个版本，保留优点并修改造成困惑的句子。反馈需要行动机会才有价值；一次评论过多也会令人负担沉重，目标应当可执行。

paragraphs.english: A striking headline appears in a class messaging group. Several students want to forward it, but one student asks where the claim came from. He opens the full article and checks the date, the author and the source. He finds that the headline leaves out an important condition. Reading beyond the first sentence can change how a claim is understood and whether it seems relevant.
paragraphs.chinese: 班群里出现吸引人的标题，一名学生在转发前打开全文，检查日期、作者和来源。他发现标题遗漏了重要条件，读完整内容后，对结论的理解发生变化。

paragraphs.english: The group compares the article with another account of the same event. They distinguish a report of what happened from a comment expressing an opinion. This does not mean that every disagreement can be resolved immediately. Sources may offer incomplete information, and verification takes time. The students decide that uncertainty is a reason to pause, rather than a reason to present a doubtful claim as a fact.
paragraphs.chinese: 大家对照另一份报道，区分事实报道与观点。来源也可能不完整，核实需要时间。面对不确定性，他们决定暂停转发，而不是把可疑说法当成事实。

paragraphs.english: People learn when they question a plan as well as follow it. They can choose a small change and share the result. The aim is to notice a benefit that matters in everyday life. A familiar headline can feel convincing before its source has been checked. Readers could compare the original report with the shared summary and note what was omitted. Finding agreement between copies is weaker than finding independent support.
paragraphs.chinese: 人们质疑计划、而非仅照做，也能学到东西。他们可以选择小改变、分享结果，目标是发现对日常生活有意义的益处。熟悉的标题可能在来源尚未核实前就令人信服。读者可以比较原始报道与分享摘要，记录被遗漏的内容。多个副本相同，不如独立来源的支持有说服力。

articles.title: Small Steps: Working Across a Distance
articles.subtitle: 远程协作中的安排、沟通与边界
articles.provenance: AI 原创分级练习 · 2026-10-12 · 情境结尾与题目修订；难度未作教学标定

paragraphs.english: A small team works from different places. To finish a shared project, its members need coordination rather than constant messages. They write down who is responsible for each task and agree on a time to discuss questions. One colleague works in a different time zone, so the meeting schedule must take that difference into account. A convenient arrangement for one person may be difficult for another.
paragraphs.chinese: 异地团队通过明确任务和讨论时间来协调，而不是不断发消息。由于成员可能处于不同时区，会议安排需要兼顾差异，不能只让某一个人方便。

paragraphs.english: The team keeps a short record of decisions so that absent colleagues can follow the discussion later. A document can reduce confusion, but it does not automatically create trust. People may still need a direct conversation when an issue is sensitive or unclear. Remote work also depends on reliable technology and suitable space. These conditions are not equally available to every worker.

paragraphs.english: An employee learns to use a new booking system at work. Her manager organises a training session and provides a short guide. After the session, she tries a realistic task with supervision. When she makes a mistake, she can ask why it happened and try again. A demonstration is helpful, but doing the task gives her a different kind of understanding.
paragraphs.chinese: 员工学习新的预订系统，先接受培训、阅读指南，再在指导下完成真实任务。犯错后询问原因并重试。观看演示与亲手操作能带来不同理解。

paragraphs.english: The manager checks whether staff have enough time to practise. An opportunity to learn may be hard to use when everyday duties leave no space for it. The organisation also asks experienced workers to share their knowledge without assuming that they will teach for free after work. Training involves time and effort as well as course material, and those costs need to be recognised.
paragraphs.chinese: 管理者检查员工是否有练习时间，也不假定资深员工应下班后无偿教学。培训需要时间和精力，不只是提供课程材料，这些投入应得到承认。

paragraphs.english: It helps to share a question before people choose what to do. They can learn whether a plan brings a benefit. Their aim may stay the same even when they change the next step. A worker may perform a task correctly beside a trainer and struggle when working alone. A later attempt under ordinary conditions would show what has been retained. It could also reveal which part of the instructions needs another example.
paragraphs.chinese: 选择行动前先分享问题会有帮助。人们可以了解计划是否带来益处；即使调整下一步，目标仍可保持。员工在培训者身边可能操作正确，独立工作时却可能遇到困难。之后在普通条件下再次尝试，可以判断保留了哪些技能，也能发现哪部分说明还需要例子。

paragraphs.english: A group of volunteers helps at a neighbourhood event. Before it begins, the organiser explains the purpose and asks what support visitors may need. One volunteer gives directions, another prepares signs, and a third helps people find a seat. A clear role makes it easier for each person to contribute. The group also knows whom to ask when a question is beyond its knowledge.
paragraphs.chinese: 社区活动前，组织者说明目的并了解访客需要。志愿者分工指路、准备标识和帮助找座位，也知道遇到超出能力的问题时向谁求助。

paragraphs.english: After the event, volunteers listen to feedback rather than assuming that a busy day was automatically a successful one. A visitor may have found the signs confusing even when the team worked hard. Enthusiasm is valuable, but it does not replace preparation or appropriate skills. A responsible project recognises the limits of volunteers and avoids giving them tasks that require expertise they do not have.
paragraphs.chinese: 活动后，大家倾听反馈，不把忙碌等同于成功。热情不能取代准备和技能，负责任的项目应承认志愿者的能力边界。

paragraphs.english: People can choose a plan and share a question before they act. The aim is to learn from what happens. A small benefit is still useful, and they can change the next step. A busy volunteer session does not automatically meet the needs of the people receiving help. Asking those people which part was useful would guide the next session. Volunteers should also know where their role ends and specialist help begins.
paragraphs.chinese: 人们可以在行动前选择计划、提出并分享问题。目标是从结果中学习，小益处也有价值，之后可以调整下一步。忙碌的志愿活动不自动意味着满足了受助者需求。询问他们哪部分有用，可以指导下一次活动。志愿者也应知道自身职责的边界，以及何时需要专业帮助。

paragraphs.english: A student wants to recycle an empty food container. Its label contains a symbol, but she is unsure whether the local collection accepts this material. She checks the council's guidance and notices that the lid and the main container follow different instructions. The symbol alone does not answer every practical question. A useful label needs to help a person connect the packaging with the system available in their area.
paragraphs.chinese: 学生想回收空食品盒，却不确定标识中的材料是否属于当地收集范围。她查阅市政指南，发现盖子与盒身需要不同处理。一个符号无法回答所有实际问题，实用标签应帮助使用者把包装与本地系统联系起来。

paragraphs.english: A neighbourhood group compares labels and asks residents which instructions they find confusing. Contamination can occur when unsuitable items enter the same collection. The group prepares examples using local guidance rather than claiming that one rule applies everywhere. Clear information may improve sorting, but information is only part of the process. A collection also needs suitable facilities, reliable transport and a destination that can actually handle the material.
paragraphs.chinese: 社区小组比较标签，询问居民哪些说明难懂。不适合的物品进入同一回收流程可能造成污染。小组依据本地指南制作例子，不声称规则全球通用。清晰信息有助分类，但流程还需要设施、可靠运输和真正能够处理材料的接收地点。

paragraphs.english: The aim is to choose a step that fits daily life. People can share a plan, ask a question and learn from the result. If the benefit is small, they can change their approach. A label may be easy to read while still pointing to a service that is unavailable locally. Residents could compare the printed instruction with the collection rules for their area. Confusion in that comparison is a design problem worth reporting.
paragraphs.chinese: 目标是选择适合日常生活的步骤。人们可以分享计划、提问并从结果中学习；益处较小时可以调整方法。标签可能容易阅读，却指向当地没有的服务。居民可以把印刷说明与本地收集规定比较。如果比较后仍有困惑，这就是值得反馈的设计问题。

articles.title: Small Steps: More Than a Lunch Menu

paragraphs.english: A school asks pupils what they think about lunchtime. Some like the menu, but others find the queue too long to enjoy the break. Staff observe how food is served and ask pupils to describe a normal day rather than an unusually good or bad one. The discussion includes variety, the time available and whether the dining space gives different pupils a comfortable place to sit.
paragraphs.chinese: 学校询问学生对午餐的看法。有的喜欢菜单，有的觉得排队太久。员工观察供餐，并请学生描述平常的一天，而非特别好或坏的例子。讨论涵盖食物种类、时间，以及不同学生能否舒服地入座。

paragraphs.english: The school tests a small change to the serving arrangement and gathers feedback before redesigning the whole service. A preference survey cannot explain every reason for a pupil's choice. Some pupils may bring food from home because of routines that the school does not see. Listening to several groups can reveal different experiences, but staff still need to connect those comments with the practical limits of space, staffing and time.
paragraphs.chinese: 学校先小幅调整供餐安排，再收集反馈，而非立刻重做整项服务。偏好调查无法解释所有选择原因，一些学生自带食物可能源于学校不了解的家庭习惯。倾听不同群体有助发现差异，但意见仍需结合空间、人手与时间限制。

paragraphs.english: It helps to share a question before people choose what to do. They can learn whether a plan brings a benefit. Their aim may stay the same even when they change the next step. Changing a menu does not ensure that pupils will eat the new meals. Listening to pupils and checking what remains on their plates would add useful evidence. The school should compare this information with the cost and practical work of serving lunch.
paragraphs.chinese: 选择行动前先分享问题会有帮助。人们可以了解计划是否带来益处；即使调整下一步，目标仍可保持。改变菜单不保证学生会吃新的饭菜。听取学生意见、检查餐盘剩余食物，可以补充有用证据。学校还应把这些信息与成本和供餐所需的实际工作比较。

paragraphs.english: A student creates a revision plan for an upcoming examination. She begins with a short practice task and records which errors she makes. paragraphs.english: After a week, she checks whether her practice resembles the tasks she will face. Memorising a model response may feel reassuring, but a question with a different focus can require a different answer. paragraphs.english: A designer reviews an online form for a local service. A participant who uses a keyboard cannot see which field is currently selected. Another person finds the instructions difficult to follow. The designer changes the navigation and writes a clearer label for each field. Accessibility becomes a question about completing a real task rather than merely adding a feature at the end of the design process.
paragraphs.chinese: 设计者检查本地服务的在线表单。一位键盘用户看不出选中了哪个输入框，另一位参与者觉得说明难懂。设计者调整导航并明确标签，把可访问性视为完成真实任务的问题，而不是设计末尾附加一个功能。

paragraphs.english: The team tests the revised form with people who use different devices and methods. Usability is not demonstrated by one designer finishing the form quickly. A participant may need a different explanation or may encounter a problem that a checklist has missed. Testing several situations can reveal barriers, but it cannot represent every future user. The team therefore provides a way to report difficulties and plans further review after the service opens.
paragraphs.chinese: 团队让使用不同设备和方法的人测试新版表单。设计者自己完成得快，并不能证明好用。参与者可能需要另一种解释，也可能发现检查清单遗漏的问题。多个情境测试仍无法代表所有未来用户，所以团队提供反馈渠道并计划上线后继续复查。

paragraphs.english: People learn when they question a plan as well as follow it. They can choose a small change and share the result. The aim is to notice a benefit that matters in everyday life. A form can pass a checklist while still confusing a person completing it. Observing people with different needs use the same form would reveal where they hesitate or need assistance. Their explanations can guide changes that a completion count cannot.
paragraphs.chinese: 人们质疑计划、而非仅照做，也能学到东西。他们可以选择小改变、分享结果，目标是发现对日常生活有意义的益处。表单可能通过检查清单，却仍让填写者困惑。观察不同需求的人使用同一表单，可以发现犹豫或需要帮助的位置。他们的解释能指导改进，而完成次数本身不能。

paragraphs.english: A training provider uses an automated system to help organise applications. The system gives each application a score based on the information supplied. A member of staff asks which criterion contributes to that score and whether missing information is treated differently from a low result. The provider wants to understand the process before relying on its output. A number can look precise without explaining how a particular person was assessed.
paragraphs.chinese: 培训机构用自动系统辅助整理申请。系统依据资料评分，员工询问哪些标准影响结果，以及缺失信息是否区别于低成绩处理。机构希望先理解流程再依赖输出，因为一个精确数字未必解释了具体申请者如何被评估。

paragraphs.english: The provider introduces an appeal route and checks examples with staff who understand the course requirements. articles.title: Small Steps: Testing a Small Business Idea
articles.subtitle: 小规模试行怎样帮助理解顾客与成本
articles.provenance: AI 原创分级练习 · 2026-10-12 · 情境结尾与题目修订；难度未作教学标定

paragraphs.english: A craft worker considers selling a new product at a weekend market. Before producing a large quantity, she prepares a prototype and asks visitors what they would use it for. Some admire its appearance, while others explain a practical difficulty. She records the comments separately from actual purchases. A positive reaction is useful information, but it is not the same as evidence that enough people will buy the product regularly.
paragraphs.chinese: 手艺人考虑在周末集市销售新产品。大量制作前，她先做样品，询问访客用途。有的喜欢外观，有的指出实际困难。她区分评论与真实购买，因为积极反应不等于足够多人会持续购买的证据。

paragraphs.english: She calculates the time spent making each item and compares revenue with the costs she can identify. Overhead expenses, such as a stall fee, also matter even when only a few products are sold. A weekend trial cannot reveal every seasonal change in demand. The worker uses it to decide which questions need a longer test, rather than treating one busy afternoon as a guarantee that the business will remain viable.
paragraphs.chinese: 她计算单件制作时间，比较收入与已识别成本。摊位费等间接开销即使销量少也存在。周末试行无法反映所有季节性需求变化，因此她用结果决定哪些问题要长期测试，而不把一个忙碌下午当成生意持续可行的保证。

paragraphs.english: The aim is to choose a step that fits daily life. People can share a plan, ask a question and learn from the result. If the benefit is small, they can change their approach. Interest in an idea is different from willingness to pay for it. A small trial could record actual purchases and the work needed to deliver them. That would help the owner judge demand before committing to a larger expense.
paragraphs.chinese: 目标是选择适合日常生活的步骤。人们可以分享计划、提问并从结果中学习；益处较小时可以调整方法。对想法感兴趣，不等于愿意付费。小规模试验可以记录实际购买，以及完成订单需要的工作，帮助经营者在投入更多费用前判断需求。

paragraphs.english: A craft worker considers selling a new product at a weekend market. Before producing a large quantity, she prepares a prototype and asks visitors what they would use it for. Some admire its appearance, while others explain a practical difficulty. She records the comments separately from actual purchases. A positive reaction is useful information, but it is not the same as evidence that enough people will buy the product regularly.
paragraphs.chinese: 手艺人考虑在周末集市销售新产品。大量制作前，她先做样品，询问访客用途。有的喜欢外观，有的指出实际困难。她区分评论与真实购买，因为积极反应不等于足够多人会持续购买的证据。

paragraphs.english: She calculates the time spent making each item and compares revenue with the costs she can identify. Overhead expenses, such as a stall fee, also matter even when only a few products are sold. A weekend trial cannot reveal every seasonal change in demand. The worker uses it to decide which questions need a longer test, rather than treating one busy afternoon as a guarantee that the business will remain viable.
paragraphs.chinese: 她计算单件制作时间，比较收入与已识别成本。摊位费等间接开销即使销量少也存在。周末试行无法反映所有季节性需求变化，因此她用结果决定哪些问题要长期测试，而不把一个忙碌下午当成生意持续可行的保证。

paragraphs.english: An effective approach connects evidence with the resources required. A significant impact alone cannot justify every investment; a sustainable change also needs to work under ordinary conditions. Interest in an idea is different from willingness to pay for it. A small trial could record actual purchases and the work needed to deliver them. That would help the owner judge demand before committing to a larger expense.
paragraphs.chinese: 有效方法把证据与所需资源联系起来。显著影响本身不能证明每项投入都合理；可持续改变还需要在普通条件下发挥作用。对想法感兴趣，不等于愿意付费。小规模试验可以记录实际购买，以及完成订单需要的工作，帮助经营者在投入更多费用前判断需求。

paragraphs.english: An apprentice joins a workshop and watches a mentor prepare a task. The mentor explains why each tool is selected instead of asking the learner to copy movements without a reason. The apprentice then performs a supervised part of the task and records questions. Observation and practice support different kinds of understanding. A useful apprenticeship gives the learner opportunities to connect an explanation with the decisions made during real work.
paragraphs.chinese: 学徒在车间观察导师准备任务。导师解释选择工具的原因，而不是要求无理由地模仿动作。学徒随后在监督下完成部分任务并记录问题。观察与练习支持不同理解，好的培训让学习者把说明与实际工作决策联系起来。

paragraphs.english: The workshop reviews progress against a clear competency rather than simply counting time spent at work. A learner may need repeated practice before completing a task independently. The mentor also recognises that a busy production schedule can reduce time for explanation. Teaching responsibilities therefore need to be planned alongside the workshop's other duties. Being present in a workplace does not automatically ensure that a person has received suitable instruction or meaningful feedback.
paragraphs.chinese: 车间依据明确能力要求检查进步，而不只统计在岗时长。学习者可能需多次练习才能独立完成任务，繁忙生产也可能挤压讲解时间。因此教学责任要与其他工作共同安排。身处工作场所并不自动意味着获得合适指导和有意义的反馈。

paragraphs.english: People learn when they question a plan as well as follow it. They can choose a small change and share the result. The aim is to notice a benefit that matters in everyday life. Watching a mentor gives an apprentice an example, but independent practice reveals different difficulties. The mentor could observe a later attempt and ask the apprentice to explain each choice. Safe supervision still matters while responsibility gradually increases.
paragraphs.chinese: 人们质疑计划、而非仅照做，也能学到东西。他们可以选择小改变、分享结果，目标是发现对日常生活有意义的益处。观察导师提供了示范，独立练习则会暴露不同困难。导师可以观察之后的尝试，请学徒解释每个选择。在责任逐步增加时，安全监督仍然重要。

paragraphs.english: A local history group records memories of a street that has changed over several decades. An interview with a former shopkeeper describes one period, while a photograph suggests another detail worth checking. The group keeps a note of where each account came from. Memory can reveal experiences that an official record does not describe, but it can also contain uncertainty about dates or the order of events.
paragraphs.chinese: 地方史小组记录一条街数十年的变化。旧店主的访谈讲述一个时期，照片又提供值得核查的细节。小组记录每项叙述来源。记忆能呈现官方记录未描述的经历，也可能在日期和事件顺序上不确定。

paragraphs.english: The group places different accounts beside one another instead of forcing them into a single seamless story. An archive may preserve more material from some groups than from others. The absence of a record does not necessarily mean that an activity never happened. The exhibition explains what is known, what remains uncertain and which voices have not yet been heard. Local history becomes more informative when the limits of its evidence are visible.
paragraphs.chinese: 小组并列不同叙述，不强行拼成毫无缝隙的故事。档案可能保存某些群体的材料更多，缺乏记录不必然代表某项活动从未发生。展览解释已知事项、不确定处与尚未听到的声音，使证据边界清晰可见。

paragraphs.english: The aim is to choose a step that fits daily life. People can share a plan, ask a question and learn from the result. If the benefit is small, they can change their approach. A collection of memories may become richer when accounts disagree. Comparing stories about the same street would show how people experienced it differently. The group should identify uncertain details rather than silently combine every account into one story.
paragraphs.chinese: 目标是选择适合日常生活的步骤。人们可以分享计划、提问并从结果中学习；益处较小时可以调整方法。记忆合集可能因叙述不一致而更加丰富。比较关于同一街道的故事，可以了解不同人的经历。团队应标明不确定细节，而不是把所有叙述悄悄合并成一个故事。

paragraphs.english: A neighbourhood receives a small budget for a shared project. Residents suggest new benches, clearer signs and equipment for a meeting room. The facilitator asks each group to explain who would benefit and what the project would require after it was completed. A proposal becomes easier to compare when its purpose, estimated cost and continuing needs are visible. The discussion includes people who may use the project less often but still contribute to it.
paragraphs.chinese: 社区收到一笔共享项目预算。居民提出长椅、标识和活动室设备等方案。主持者请各组说明谁受益、完成后还需要什么。当目的、估计成本与持续需要都明确时，方案更易比较。讨论也纳入使用较少但仍会参与投入的人。

paragraphs.english: The group publishes its selection criteria and offers a way to submit comments outside the meeting. A vote can show the preferences of those who participate, but it does not automatically represent everyone in the neighbourhood. Some residents may find the process difficult to access. The group therefore reviews participation as well as the final result and explains why the chosen project was prioritised over the alternatives that were proposed.
paragraphs.chinese: 小组公布选择标准，提供会外提交意见的渠道。投票显示参加者的偏好，却不会自动代表所有居民，因为部分人可能难以参与。团队因此同时检查参与过程与结果，并解释所选项目为何优先于其他方案。

paragraphs.english: People learn when they question a plan as well as follow it. They can choose a small change and share the result. The aim is to notice a benefit that matters in everyday life. A popular proposal may receive many votes while meeting only one group's needs. Comparing participation across the community would help explain whose preferences the result represents. The next discussion could seek views from people who did not take part.
paragraphs.chinese: 人们质疑计划、而非仅照做，也能学到东西。他们可以选择小改变、分享结果，目标是发现对日常生活有意义的益处。受欢迎的方案可能获得很多票，却只满足某一群体的需求。比较社区不同人群的参与情况，可以解释结果代表了谁的偏好。之后的讨论可以听取未参与者的意见。
